hints: Start by thinking about the lock and key analogy. Which part is the rigid lock with a fixed shape, and which part is the key that must fit exactly?
Focus on shapes. What must be true about the shape of the peptidoglycan substrate compared to the shape of the lysozyme active site in this old model?
Think about the end of the reaction. What should your final diagram show to prove the lysozyme is unchanged and the substrate has been split by hydrolysis?
walkthrough:
Draw the Separate Lock and Key**
Think of lysozyme as a large protein with a small hollow called the active site. In the lock and key model this active site has a fixed, rigid, specific shape that does not change. Draw lysozyme as a large shape with a notch cut out, label it lysozyme and label the notch active site. Then draw peptidoglycan nearby as a smaller shape with a complementary protruding shape that fits exactly, and label it peptidoglycan or substrate or murein. This complementarity is the whole idea of lock and key.

Show the Enzyme-Substrate Complex**
Now draw the key in the lock. Place the peptidoglycan neatly inside the active site of lysozyme with the shapes touching exactly. Label this enzyme-substrate complex. You can annotate to say shapes are complementary, so substrate fits precisely into active site. Do not show the active site changing shape, that would be induced fit, which this question specifically says not to use.

Show Unchanged Enzyme Plus Products**
Finally draw lysozyme released with exactly the same shaped active site as at the start, to show enzyme is unchanged and reusable. Next to it draw the peptidoglycan split into two smaller pieces, and label them NAG and NAM. Annotate to say hydrolysis of glycosidic bonds has occurred, using water. Common pitfall: you can score max 2 if you draw a perfect generic lock and key but forget the specific labels lysozyme, peptidoglycan or murein, NAG and NAM. You can score max 1 if you draw with no labels at all, so labelling is essential for all 3 marks.

Final answer: Diagram showing: lysozyme enzyme with a specifically shaped active site; complementary shaped peptidoglycan substrate binding into active site to form an enzyme-substrate complex; hydrolysed products (NAG and NAM) leaving the active site with the lysozyme enzyme unchanged.

hints: Start with the outcome for the bacterium. What happens to the strength of the cell wall and then to the whole cell when either agent acts?
Now think about what kind of molecule each agent is and what it actually does. One breaks bonds, the other stops bonds being made. Which is which?
For a difference, ask when each can work. Does stopping new wall synthesis matter if the bacterium is not growing, compared to breaking an existing wall?
walkthrough:
State the Similarity, Both Cause Lysis**
Both lysozyme and penicillin are antibacterial because they weaken or destroy the peptidoglycan cell wall. With a weak wall, the cell cannot withstand internal turgor pressure as water enters by osmosis, so the cell bursts, a process called lysis. Note: do not just write they kill bacteria, you must link wall damage to lysis for the mark.

Explain the Different Mechanisms**
Lysozyme is a protein enzyme and biological catalyst that hydrolyses glycosidic bonds in existing peptidoglycan molecules. Penicillin is different, it is a small antibiotic molecule, a beta-lactam, that acts as an enzyme inhibitor. It inhibits transpeptidase enzymes, so peptide cross bridges or cross linkages between peptidoglycan chains cannot form. In short, lysozyme breaks old wall, penicillin prevents new wall cross-linking.

Give Another Clear Difference**
Because penicillin only prevents formation of new cross-links, it is only effective when cells are growing and synthesising new walls. It cannot repair holes made by autolysins in a non-growing cell. Lysozyme can hydrolyse existing wall at any stage, so it is effective even on non-growing bacteria. Exam tip: you must attempt both similarities and differences to gain full 3 marks, so write at least one similarity point about lysis and at least one or two difference points about mechanism or timing.

Final answer: Similarities: both cause bacterial cell lysis / bursting by weakening the peptidoglycan cell wall so it cannot withstand turgor pressure. Differences: lysozyme is an enzyme that hydrolyses existing beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds at any stage, whereas penicillin is an antibiotic / enzyme inhibitor that inhibits transpeptidase to prevent cross-link formation only in growing bacteria.
